title: The Fed rate cycle: from restriction to reaction
deck: A framework for reading the policy function when inflation, employment, and financial conditions are sending different signals.
author: NEXUS Macro Desk
takeaway: The next move is less important than the reaction function. Policy is restrictive, but the distribution around neutral has widened.

sections.title: The rate is not the regime
sections.body: The federal funds rate is a level; the regime is the committee’s tolerance for growth and inflation variance. Markets routinely price the former while missing the latter.

sections.title: Why term premium matters now
sections.body: Long rates can stay elevated even as the policy rate falls. A larger fiscal supply, uncertain inflation path, and more volatile growth distribution all appear in the term premium.

sections.title: The practical signal set
sections.body: Read payroll revisions, bank lending surveys, and services inflation together. A single monthly print should move the forecast only when it changes the underlying story.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.summary: Disinflation resumes and a soft landing unlocks a measured easing path.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.summary: The committee waits for confirmation; real rates stay positive.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.summary: Services inflation re-accelerates and the easing window closes.
